title: cohorted-warmup-replayer-and-token-hotpath-tracer
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a cohort-aware warmup replayer that generates epochal warmup sequences per-cohort, plus an optional lightweight token-level hotpath tracer and a quantile-stratified summary exporter. Improves cold-start tail stability for mixed sequence workloads; no breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: benchmarking long-tail cold starts and per-cohort variability in token-serving hotpaths is difficult with global replayers. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a Cohorted Warmup Replayer that runs short epochal warmup sessions per user/workload cohort to produce realistic KV-cache warm states, and (2) a Token Hotpath Tracer that records lightweight per-token timing buckets to map hotspots to kernels. Together these enable quantile-stratified export reports that are much better at reproducing p99+p999 tail behaviors in heterogeneous mixes.

What I changed (single-string summary, with checklist):
- Implemented a cohorted warmup engine that groups traces by sequence shape and recent latency signature; epochs are triggered before main replay batches.
- Added a token hotpath tracer that samples token emission timing (microsecond buckets) and annotates traces with kernel hints (when available).
- Built a quantile-stratified exporter that merges cohort epoch stats into reports consumable by existing reporting pipelines.
- Integration tests and a small local end-to-end harness for reproducing p95/p99 regressions.
- Docs: benchlab README update with example experiment config and cohort definitions.

Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration harness, [x] local perf microbench, [x] docs updated, [x] Linear items linked.

Design notes and rationale: the replayer runs short warmup epochs sized to median sequence length of the cohort to avoid over-warming high-cost long sequences while still priming KV caches for typical tails. Cohorts are defined by a small set of attributes (sequence length bucket, average tokens/sec observed, and template fingerprint). The token tracer samples 1 in N tokens (configurable) and records emission time deltas in coarse microsecond buckets plus an optional kernel-hint tag when the runtime exposes the kernel selection. This keeps overhead <2% in microbench runs.

Review thread (abridged):
- Diego Morales (reviewer): "Nice approach. Two questions: 1) how stable are cohorts across deployments? 2) Can we avoid storing tracer payloads in-memory for long runs?"
- Maya Patel (author): "1) cohorts default to ephemeral per-run but we persist cohort fingerprints in the report to allow cross-run mapping; we can add a persisted catalog if needed. 2) tracer payloads are streamed to the exporter; we keep a small ring buffer and flush on epoch boundary. See benchlab/replayers/cohorted_warmup.py lines 212-245 for the ring buffer impl."
- Eileen Zhang (reviewer): "CI flakes on the e2e job in the first run. I ran locally and saw an intermittent timing assertion in test_token_hotpath — likely due to timer resolution on macOS. Can you add a small relaxation?"
- Maya Patel: "Added a 10us slack in timer assertions and moved the test to use a deterministic fake-timer in CI-only path. PTAL."
- Ravi Singh (reviewer): "Question on exporter schema: downstream dashboards expect 'cohort_id' and we now emit 'cohort_fingerprint'. Is that mapped?"
- Maya: "Added a compatibility shim in quantile_stratified.py that emits both cohort_id (stable hash) and cohort_fingerprint. Updated docs section."

CI summary and reruns: initial CI run (linux-build/test) failed on bench-e2e (timing assertion). After test fix and rebase, CI passed. Bench-e2e is gated to optional workflow to avoid blocking main merges; nightly scheduled runs collect epochal outputs. Final CI status: pass (all required checks green).

Performance notes from local microbench: in a mixed sequence workload (60/30/10 short/med/long) with cohorted warmup enabled, tail p99 reduced by ~18% and p999 by ~9% compared to baseline global replayer; median unaffected. Token tracer overhead measured ~1.6% in a 10k request microbench with sampling 1:50.

Compatibility and rollout: feature is behind a feature-flag in benchlab config (warmup.cohorted.enabled, tracer.enabled). Default flags are off to ensure reproducibility. We plan to enable the warmup replayer in nightly benchmark runs for two weeks and then promote to CI gated experiments if stable.

Follow-ups (tracked in Linear):

Merge outcome: squashed and merged by Maya Patel via squash merge on 2026-02-24. Release note added to benchlab CHANGELOG under unreleased.

Notes for reviewers/maintainers: this PR intentionally keeps runtime hooks optional and lightweight. If we see any regressions in nightly runs, the feature flags make it trivial to roll back. The documentation contains an analysis notebook and an example that reproduces the local microbench numbers.
